sources.note: Audits four neuroscience-inspired claims about language models across 17 checkpoints from five families and 0.6B to 72B, and shows that an apparent emergence of concept steerability with scale is produced entirely by uncalibrated measurement -- raw intervention units, the readout metric, and a fixed operating point -- with correcting any one of the three removing the trend.
sources.title: When Is a Steerable Concept Representation Real? Measurement Confounds in a Cross-Family Audit of Neuroscience Parallels in LLMs

sources.note: Builds an expert-annotated Indian Supreme Court dataset in which each applicable statute is paired with the specific text span a legal expert says establishes it, and uses it to show that predicting the right statute and giving the right reason are separable abilities.
sources.title: PROSLEX: A Novel Dataset for Expert-Annotated Legal Statute Prediction for Indian Judiciary

sources.note: Defines certaindex, an algorithm-agnostic measure of how much a reasoning algorithm's answer has stopped changing, and builds it into a serving system that reallocates or terminates compute per query — saving up to 50% of tokens in batch inference and tripling online throughput.
sources.title: Efficiently Scaling LLM Reasoning with Certaindex

sources.note: Turns each intermediate step of a reasoning trajectory into a numerical feature vector of distances to the answer choices, projects those into 2D to visualize how trajectories move through answer space, and reuses the same features to build a lightweight verifier for weighted voting.
sources.title: Landscape of Thoughts: Visualizing the Reasoning Process of Large Language Models

result.definition: A 70B Llama, used across 4 sources as the large open model in cross-scale audits and serving studies. Its measured appearances: as the top of a cross-family steering audit's large-model grid, where it shows a significant positive effect of +4.5 under the full protocol -- one of the five models above 24B establishing that steering neither emerges nor collapses with scale; as the model in a reasoning-trajectory visualisation with accuracies of 84.4, 80.2, 75.8 and 64.8 percent across four tasks; and as a subject in adaptive serving and legal-explanation work.
